entries.rule: Status table: same/retro is agreement in direction, with how far off recorded in magnitude; contra is a wrong prediction. Precedent adjudications keep direction as the status test.
entries.adjudication_note: Status table and retrodiction rule: model predicted a viral-load decline and paritaprevir patients declined; direction agrees, under-prediction (1.9 vs 4.07 log10) goes in magnitude off_by_>5x. Reproduced the known result: retro, as lomibuvir precedent.

entries.rule: Status table: same/retro is agreement in direction, with how far off recorded in magnitude; contra is a wrong prediction. Precedent adjudications keep direction as the status test.
entries.adjudication_note: Status table and retrodiction rule: predicted decline (2.2 log10) matched danoprevir's observed decline (3.9) in direction; authors' 'poor candidate' is a magnitude miss, recorded as off_by_>5x. Retro, consistent with lomibuvir precedent.

missing: Efficacy: vaniprevir phase II (Manns 2012 Hepatology, doi:10.1002/hep.25743, epub 2012-07-17): primary endpoint RVR 68.8-83.3% vs 5.6% placebo (P<0.001). An earlier member 'same' (paired with vaniprevir replicon data), so the efficacy cell turns 'same' in 2012, not 2013.

Dose: glecaprevir 6-month rat NOAEL gives a 70x exposure margin at 300 mg (209394 PharmR: 'This provides an exposure margin of 70X'), which held in patients. This is a margin_stated 'same' (2017) and could carry the dose cell if dose entry 2 is not accepted.

Safety (no status change expected): FDA clinical hold on sovaprevir, June 2013, for grade 3-4 ALT elevations in a healthy-volunteer DDI study with atazanavir/ritonavir (Achillion 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1070336/000119312514089075/d645073d10k.htm; https://www.fiercepharma.com/regulatory/fda-slaps-a-clinical-hold-on-achillion-hep-c-drug). The harm came from conditions the model never tested, so 'untested'; the draft's judgement should mention it.
rule_questions: Dose table 'reached, drug worked': does a phase 1 viral-load response count as 'worked', so the entry is dated at phase 1, or must the efficacy primary endpoint have read out first? Also, can a dose entry be 'same' when the source never reports exposure against the model's numeric target (EC99)?
Q80K: the replicon fold change was measured on baseline clinical isolates at the same time as the phase 3 trials. Is this a prospective model prediction or a retrodiction (retro)?

Hepatotoxicity seen only under a drug interaction (sovaprevir with atazanavir/r in healthy volunteers; paritaprevir with ethinyl estradiol): no rule says whether a DDI-driven harm the animals were never dosed under counts as the model's silence being contradicted or as untested.

Models check: a routine preclinical model (HCV chimpanzee monotherapy) whose run date is unstated and whose first record (2010) post-dates a public patient result (AASLD 2008), but which was not motivated by it. Rule 10 requires both 'post-dates' and 'motivated by'; scored retro here on the record date.

VK-model tracks (Reddy 2012): an in-silico magnitude prediction that is right in direction but under-predicts a potent drug by >1.5 log10 (danoprevir, paritaprevir) is scored contra because the authors call it a misjudged candidate, while simeprevir over-predicted by 1.3 log10 is retro. The rules define same/retro by direction only; confirm whether a source's own 'miss' call on magnitude makes contra.
